 MVSU Delta Devils vs Oregon Ducks Prediction, 11/11/2026 College Basketball Picks, Best Bets & Odds
 by Guy Bruhn - 11/10/2026 
 Game: MVSU Delta Devils vs Oregon Ducks
 Date: Wednesday, November 11, 2026
 Location: Matthew Knight Arena in Eugene, OR
 TV: B1G+
 The Oregon Ducks (2-0) are welcoming the MVSU Delta Devils (0-2) at Matthew Knight Arena on Wednesday.
 The MVSU Delta Devils faced off with Washington and went home with a loss by a final score of 77-64 in their last game. MVSU wrapped up the contest with a 36.5% field goal percentage (19 of 52) and converted 7 out of their 22 shots from beyond the arc. At the free throw line, the Delta Devils knocked down 19 of their 23 attempts for a percentage of 82.6%. Regarding rebounding, they earned 24 with 5 of them being offensive. They also recorded 8 assists in the matchup while forcing the other team into 13 turnovers and earning 8 steals. When it comes to defending, MVSU allowed their opponent to shoot 41.8% from the field on 28 out of 67 shooting. Washington recorded 23 assists and had 6 steals in this matchup. In addition, Washington pulled down 46 boards (16 offensive, 30 defensive), but wasn't able to record a block. Washington finished shooting 57.1% at the free throw line by burying 4 of 7 attempts. They also knocked down 17 out of their 50 shots from distance. In relation to personal fouls, the Delta Devils finished with 10 while Washington accumulated 15 personal fouls.
 AJ Abrams is a guy who came through in this contest. He finished the game at 71.4% from the floor and also distributed 1 assist. He played for 29 mins and totaled 6 rebounds. He ended up finishing with 20 points on 5 out of 7 shooting.

 MVSU comes into this game with a record of 0-2 for the campaign. They average 60.5 points per contest (345th in Division 1) while connecting on 36.4% from the floor. The Delta Devils are hitting 25.0% on shots from beyond the arc (10 of 40) and 79.5% from the charity stripe. As a team, MVSU is collecting 28.5 boards per contest and has earned 16 assists this season, which has them ranked 360th in college in terms of passing the rock. They are turning it over 12.5 times per contest and as a team they are committing 9.5 fouls every game.
 Defensively, the Delta Devils are able to force 12.5 turnovers per contest and they draw 14.5 fouls. They relinquish 33.3% on 3-pointers and they are 284th in Division 1 in opponents PPG (80.5). The Delta Devils are allowing a field goal percentage of 44.5% (61 of 137) and they surrender 44.0 boards per game as a team. They are ranked 333rd in D-1 in giving up assists with 48 surrendered on the year.
 The last time they took the court, the Oregon Ducks walked away with a victory by a final of 98-71 when they faced Eastern Washington. The Ducks earned 28 defensive boards and 9 offensive rebounds totaling 37 for the matchup. They also gave up possession 13 times, while getting 11 steals in this contest. Eastern Washington earned 17 fouls in this contest which got the Ducks to the charity stripe for 15 attempts. They were able to knock down 11 of the free throw tries for a rate of 73.3%. In regard to 3-point attempts, Oregon converted 9 of their 25 tries (36.0%). When this game wrapped up, the Ducks ended up shooting 39 for 65 from the field which gave them a rate of 60.0%. The Ducks allowed Eastern Washington to make 26 of 58 tries from the floor which had them sitting at 44.8% for the contest. They wrapped up this game 23.8% from 3-point land by hitting 5 of 21 and finished the contest at 14 of 23 at the charity stripe (60.9%). In relation to how they cleaned up the glass, Oregon permitted Eastern Washington to pull down 21 in all (7 on the offensive glass).
 Wei Lin was important for the Ducks in the game. He buried 7 out of 9 for the contest for a field goal percentage of 77.8%, but wasn't able to grab a board. He accumulated 20 points in his 21 mins on the court and totaled 4 dimes in the matchup.
 Oregon has a win-loss record of 2-0 for the season. As an offense, the Ducks are shooting 60.2% from the field, which ranks 4th in Division 1. Oregon has scored 185 points so far this season (92.5 per contest) and they collect 37.5 rebounds per game. They are earning an assist 23.5 times per game (14th in college) and they are turning it over 11.0 times per game. The Ducks are responsible for committing 17.5 fouls per contest and they connect on 67.6% from the charity stripe.
 The Ducks on defense are ranked 173rd in D-1 in points per game surrendered with 70.0. They are forcing 11.5 turnovers per game and allow teams to shoot 41.4% from the floor (181st in college). The Oregon defense allows 35.3% on three-point shots (18 of 51) and their opponents are converting on 70.3% of their shots from the free throw line. They give up 15.0 dimes and 25.0 boards per contest, which is ranked 269th and 9th in D-1.
 Who will win tonight's NCAA game against the spread?
 Guy Bruhn's Pick: Take Oregon
